findings.title: forEach(async) does not await calendar/video deletions before sending reschedule email
findings.body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... }) at line 125 is the classic forEach-doesn't-await-async-callbacks anti-pattern. The function reaches line 143 (await sendRequestRescheduleEmail) and then returns while the awaited getCalendar/deleteEvent/deleteMeeting calls inside the forEach are still in flight. The reschedule email is sent before the previous calendar/video events are actually deleted, so users can get a "please reschedule" email with the original time still marked busy on the calendar. Additionally, the surrounding try/catch (lines 124 and 135-139) silently breaks: pre-PR getCalendar was synchronous so its thrown errors reached this catch, but now getCalendar returns a rejected promise from inside the async callback, so rejections become unhandled promise rejections and are never logged via logger.error.

findings.title: forEach(async) does not await calendar/video deletions before sending reschedule email
findings.body: Same bug as packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... }) does not await its async callback. The function proceeds to await sendRequestRescheduleEmail (line 143) and returns while the calendar/video deletions are still pending. The pre-existing try/catch on lines 124/135-139 also loses its ability to catch errors thrown from getCalendar, since those errors are now inside rejected promises returned by the async callback rather than synchronous throws.

findings.title: forEach(async) for recurring calendar deletions races with Promise.all(apiDeletes)
findings.body: In the recurring cancellation branch, bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { ... }) is used. Each iteration awaits getCalendar and calendar.deleteEvent and pushes the resolved result into apiDeletes. forEach does not await these async callbacks, so when the later Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) at line 652 runs, the array may not yet contain all the entries (or any of them). Even when entries are eventually pushed, they are the already-resolved values from `await calendar?.deleteEvent(...)`, not pending promises, so Promise.all provides no concurrency waiting. This means recurring calendar cancellations can be silently dropped and apiDeletes can be resolved before the actual deletions occur.

findings.title: forEach(async) does not await calendar/video deletions before reschedule email and webhook
findings.body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... }) at line 553 starts calendar and video deletions but does not wait for them. The mutation immediately proceeds to await sendRequestRescheduleEmail (line 570) and then runs sendWebhooks via Promise.all (line 618). Recipients can receive the reschedule email and webhook while the original calendar/video event is still active. Errors from getCalendar or deleteEvent/deleteMeeting inside the async callback also become unhandled promise rejections because there is no try/catch and the forEach ignores the returned promises.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials now leaks Promise<Calendar|null> in its return values without being async
findings.body: getCalendarCredentials (line 23) is still declared synchronous, but inside it calls the now-async getCalendar and stores the returned Promise<Calendar | null> in each result's `calendar` field (line 28). The only caller, getConnectedCalendars, happens to do `const calendar = await item.calendar;` so it works at runtime, but the function's signature and ReturnType no longer reflect the new shape. Any future caller that forgets to await `item.calendar` will silently get a Promise where it expects a Calendar. The function should either be marked `async`, or resolve the calendars up front with `await Promise.all(...)` before returning, so the contract matches the name.
